No spam - genuine quotes from vetted UK engine specialists only. 8,000+ Engine Codes 40+ Car Brands 100% Free · No Obligation Make Select Make Series Model Select a model Year Select Model First Engine Code Get Free Engine Quotes At a glance · what your oil consumption means Match the consumption rate to the likely cause 0.5L per 1,000 miles Moderate, monitor Low £0 (monitoring) 1L per 1,000 miles Concerning, get diagnosis Medium £50-£150 1L per 500 miles or less Serious, repair likely High £500-£4,000+ Blue smoke + oil consumption Piston rings or valve seals High £500-£4,000+ Consumption + oil light Risk of engine seizure Critical £2,500-£10,000+ What this usually means in UK cars Excessive oil consumption is the hidden problem Unlike smoke or noises, it often goes unnoticed until it's too late. In our 24,650 quote dataset, we identified three primary causes: Valve stem seals - 40% of cases Oil leaks past worn seals when the engine is off. Consumption often 1L per 1,000 miles. Repair: £500-£1,500. Piston rings - 45% of cases Worn rings allow oil past the pistons during combustion. Consumption often 1L per 500 miles or less. Repair: £1,500-£4,000+. PCV system - 10% of cases Faulty positive crankcase ventilation. Repair: £100-£200. Turbo seals - 5% of cases Oil passing through turbo bearings. Repair: £450-£3,000+. The critical rule: Any oil consumption of 1L per 1,000 miles or more requires investigation. The consequences of ignoring it are catastrophic - bearing damage, catalytic converter failure, and engine seizure. Common affected vehicles & engines Oil consumption issues by make and model Vehicle Common Engine Code Typical Oil Consumption Issue Cost Range BMW 3-Series (E90/E92) N43/N53 2.0 Valve stem seals £800-£1,500 BMW 5-Series (E60) N52 3.0 Valve seals, oil filter housing £500-£1,500 VW Golf / Audi A3 EA888 2.0 TSI Piston rings (TSI) £1,500-£3,500 Ford Focus 1.0 EcoBoost Wet belt degradation £800-£1,500 Mini Cooper N14 1.6 Piston rings £1,500-£3,500 Audi A4 / A6 EA113 2.0 TFSI PCV valve, valve seals £100-£1,500 Mercedes C-Class M271 1.8 Timing chain and oil consumption £800-£2,000 Subaru Forester EJ25 2.5 Piston rings (boxer engine) £1,500-£4,000+ What people think vs reality The expensive mistake is assuming it's normal ✕ “A little oil consumption is normal for an older car.” Some consumption is expected, but 1L per 1,000 miles is excessive and needs investigation. ✕ “I'll just keep topping it up - it's cheaper than fixing it.” You're masking the problem. Burning oil damages your catalytic converter (£500-£2,000). ✕ “Thicker oil will stop the consumption.” Thicker oil may reduce consumption temporarily but masks the underlying wear. ✕ “The garage just wants to sell me an expensive repair.” Oil consumption always gets worse. The repair costs escalate the longer you wait. This simple habit can save you £5,000+. It may help temporarily but masks the underlying issue. Always use the manufacturer-recommended oil viscosity. How much does piston ring replacement cost in the UK? blocks.question: How much oil consumption is normal?
blocks.answer: Most manufacturers consider up to 0.5L per 1,000 miles acceptable. Anything above 1L per 1,000 miles needs investigation.

blocks.question: Can I use thicker oil to reduce consumption?
blocks.answer: It may help temporarily but masks the underlying issue. Always use the manufacturer-recommended oil viscosity.

blocks.question: How much does piston ring replacement cost in the UK?
blocks.answer: Piston ring replacement costs £1,500-£4,000+. The engine must be stripped down to access the pistons.

blocks.question: Will oil consumption fail an MOT?
blocks.answer: If there's visible blue smoke from the exhaust, yes. Otherwise, it may pass but the emissions test will show elevated hydrocarbons.
